$comment: Everyday stories, noun Screen, part 3 of 4 (autoPanel, autoPanelSurface, autoPanelDataSource, workbenchAction, workbenchActionApplyTo, workbenchBandPicker, transactionHooks, transactionDerivedField, transactionUiState). Same style rules as stories-pilot.json. Owner reviews each part.

stories.autoPanel.aggregate: A goods receipt is not one row: it has a header and many lines, and the clerk works on them together. Aggregate names the main concept of that bundle, and NPDev generates the panel that opens the whole bundle as one workbench.
stories.autoPanel.concept: A shop wants a back-office page for its customers without drawing it by hand. Concept names the kind of record NPDev generates the panel for. Give either a concept or an aggregate.
stories.autoPanel.detail: When staff open one customer, they see a page with that customer's details. Detail holds the settings of that page, the surface that shows a single record.
stories.autoPanel.metadata: Whoever set up the generated panel wants to leave a note, such as 'requested by support'. Metadata is a free notebook on the panel. NPDev carries it along unchanged and does nothing with it.
stories.autoPanel.name: A generated back-office panel still needs a name, such as 'Customers'. Name is that handle. If you leave it out, NPDev derives one from the concept or aggregate.
stories.autoPanel.prompt: While filling an order, the clerk presses 'Choose customer' and a small list opens. Prompt holds the settings of that row picker, which the other pages of the panel use.
stories.autoPanel.route: Staff want to bookmark the customers page. Route is the last piece of its address, such as '/customers', the one the panel is served at.
stories.autoPanel.selection: The first thing staff see in the back office is the list of customers, from which they pick one. Selection holds the settings of that list of rows.
stories.autoPanel.surfaces: A generated panel can offer a list, a detail page, a transaction workbench and a row picker. Surfaces lists which of the four to generate. If you say nothing, the usual ones for that kind of panel are made.
stories.autoPanel.transaction: A goods receipt is edited as a whole, header and lines on one page. Transaction holds the settings of that workbench, the surface for working on a whole bundle.
stories.autoPanelDataSource.procedure: The list of 'best customers' is not stored anywhere, it is worked out. Procedure names a declared flow whose answer becomes the rows of this list.
stories.autoPanelSurface.actions: On the goods receipt workbench there are buttons like 'Recalculate' and 'Suggest location'. Actions declares them in a typed way, so a typo in a key is caught when the model is checked, not when the button silently does nothing.
stories.autoPanelSurface.bandPickers: On a receipt, the clerk adds lines by choosing from a list of products in a pop-up. Band pickers declares one such pop-up for each list of lines, named after that list. A picker may use a ready-made selection panel, or only a filter and multi-select.
stories.autoPanelSurface.columns: The list of customers should show name, city and balance, in that order. Columns lists what this page shows as columns.
stories.autoPanelSurface.computed: A list of orders could also show 'days open', which is not stored but worked out. Computed adds such read-only columns, each one a column name, an expression and the list it belongs to. They are calculated live.
stories.autoPanelSurface.dataSource: The list of customers normally reads the customers stored in the database. Data source replaces that supply, for instance with a flow's answer, for the list surface.
stories.autoPanelSurface.derivedFields: While the clerk edits the receipt, a total at the top should update with every change. Derived fields are such display-only values, worked out from the draft being edited and named by field. Nothing is stored by them.
stories.autoPanelSurface.fields: The page for one customer should show name, tax number and address, in that order. Fields lists the boxes this page shows.
stories.autoPanelSurface.filters: Staff want to narrow the customer list by city and by status. Filters lists the boxes people can filter by on this page.
stories.autoPanelSurface.hooks: A goods receipt must be checked before it is saved and a message sent after. Hooks groups those moments, the checks and calls around the workbench's save. Their own story is under the hooks keywords.
stories.autoPanelSurface.labelField: When a row appears in a pick list, 'Customer 4711' says little, but 'Ana Souza' does. Label field names the box used as the text of a row in a prompt or a selection.
stories.autoPanelSurface.layout: The customer list can be a plain table or a set of cards, one per customer. Layout picks table, which is the default, or grid, which draws each row as a card with one line per chosen column. It applies to the selection list only.
stories.autoPanelSurface.metadata: Whoever tuned this page wants to keep a note beside it. Metadata is a free notebook on the surface. NPDev carries it along unchanged and does nothing with it.
stories.autoPanelSurface.panel: The generated customer list is almost right, but the team wants to draw its own. Panel names a hand-declared panel that takes the place of the generated one. NPDev then skips generating that page, and everything that pointed to it uses yours.
stories.autoPanelSurface.regions: On the receipt workbench, the header and each list of lines is a region, and one of them could be filled by a hand-made piece. Regions says how each region is filled, by its address taken from the bundle's own tree, such as 'header' or 'items'. The addresses are never invented, only referred to.
stories.autoPanelSurface.uiState: The receipt page has a toggle, 'show details', that only changes how things look. Ui state declares such temporary choices by name, so conditions on that page can read them. They are never saved with the receipt.
stories.autoPanelSurface.visibleWhen: The 'Bank details' region of a receipt makes sense only for supplier receipts. Visible when gives conditions per region, such as 'items' shown only while the type is not cancelled. A condition can read the receipt's own boxes and the page's temporary choices.
stories.transactionHooks.beforeAction: Before the 'Post receipt' button does anything, something should check that the dock is free. Before action is a guard flow that runs first. If it answers not ok, the action is cancelled and nothing is called.
stories.transactionHooks.onCommit: After a receipt is saved, a message should go out to the buyer. On commit names the flow that runs after the save.
stories.transactionHooks.onFieldChange: Each time the clerk changes a quantity, the totals should be recalculated. On field change names a flow that is called, with a short pause, on every cell edit. The state it returns patches the draft.
stories.transactionHooks.onLoad: When a receipt opens, some values should already be filled from the purchase order. On load names a flow called once, after the draft is first loaded and before it is drawn. What it returns becomes the starting draft.
stories.transactionHooks.onValidate: Before a receipt is saved, a rule should check that quantities match the order. On validate names the flow that runs before the save. If it fails, the save is refused.
stories.transactionDerivedField.expression: The total at the top of the receipt is quantity times price, summed. Expression is the short formula, worked out by the browser, over the draft being edited. It is used by the client kind.
stories.transactionDerivedField.label: A derived number alone means little, so the screen says 'Receipt total' next to it. Label is the caption of that value.
stories.transactionDerivedField.procedure: Some totals are too heavy to work out in the browser, such as a freight cost that depends on tariffs. Procedure names the flow that is called over the draft for the value. It is used by the server kind.
stories.transactionDerivedField.tier: A simple total can be worked out right in the browser as the clerk types, while a complex one needs the server. Tier chooses client, which is the default and uses the expression, or server, which uses the flow.
stories.transactionUiState.default: The receipt page opens with the 'Summary' view already chosen. Default is the value the control starts with. If you say nothing, the first of the values is used.
stories.transactionUiState.label: A little switch on the receipt page, 'View', lets the clerk change how things are shown. Label is the caption of that control.
stories.transactionUiState.values: The 'View' switch offers 'Summary' and 'Detail' and nothing else. Values is that closed list. A condition on the page may only compare against one of them, so a typo is caught early.
stories.workbenchAction.afterAction: After 'Suggest location' runs, the draft has to take in what the flow found. After action is a flow that receives the draft and the result and returns a patched draft. It is more general than apply to, so prefer it.
stories.workbenchAction.applyTo: 'Suggest location' finds a free shelf, and the receipt should get a new line with it. Apply to folds the flow's result into the draft as a new row of a list of lines.
stories.workbenchAction.checkBalances: A clerk wants to know right now whether the debits and credits of a journal entry match, without saving. Check balances names the balance rules to test against the current draft and shows a report. It calls no flow and stores nothing, and it cannot be combined with Procedure.
stories.workbenchAction.inputFields: Before 'Split pallet' can run, the clerk must say into how many parts. Input fields lists the simple values NPDev asks the person for before calling the flow.
stories.workbenchAction.label: 'Suggest location' is clearer than the technical name of the flow behind the button. Label is the caption on the button. If you leave it out, the flow's name is used.
stories.workbenchAction.procedure: The logic of 'Suggest location' is written once as a flow. Procedure names it, and the button calls it over the draft being edited. It cannot be combined with check balances.
stories.workbenchAction.review: A helper proposes ten changes to a receipt and the clerk wants to accept only some. Review shows the result as a list of proposed changes, field by field, and only the ticked ones enter the draft. Nothing is saved until the clerk saves. It cannot be combined with apply to, after action or check balances.
stories.workbenchAction.visibleWhen: A button 'Dispatch' makes sense only on dispatch receipts. Visible when is a condition on the page, for example on the receipt's type. The button is shown only while it holds.
stories.workbenchActionApplyTo.collection: When 'Suggest location' answers, the new row must go into the right list, such as the receipt's lines. Collection names that list in the draft.
stories.workbenchActionApplyTo.map: The flow returns a shelf id, but the new line expects a box called 'location'. Map says, box by box, where each value comes from in the flow's answer. The map pairs the target box with a source path.
stories.workbenchActionApplyTo.mode: Apply to knows one way of folding a result: it adds a row at the end. Mode names it, and 'append row' is the only one implemented. For anything else, use an after action flow.
stories.workbenchBandPicker.columns: When the clerk picks a product to add as a line, the pop-up should show code, name and stock. Columns lists what the picker shows.
stories.workbenchBandPicker.filter: Only products of the supplier on the receipt should be offered. Filter is a condition made of simple tests joined by 'and', and the server enforces it. A value may read the receipt's own header, such as the supplier.
stories.workbenchBandPicker.label: The button that opens the product pop-up says 'Add products'. Label is the caption of that button.
stories.workbenchBandPicker.multiSelect: Adding twenty products one pop-up at a time is slow. Multi-select lets the clerk tick several rows in the picker and add them all at once.
stories.workbenchBandPicker.panel: The pop-up shows a ready-made list of products. Panel names the selection panel that the client offers as the modal row picker.
stories.workbenchBandPicker.selectorRef: A picker screen for products already exists with its columns, filters, order and conditions. Selector ref names it, and the picker adopts all of it. If this picker has its own filter, both are joined with 'and'.
